Core reproduced: asset_group_final_urls = ["https://roscap.co.uk"]; curl https://roscap.co.uk returns 301 to https://www.roscap.co.uk/ and curl -L counts exactly 1 redirect; the 301 preserves the query string (gad_source, gad_campaignid and gbraid are carried into the Location header, tested on / and /contact-us), so attribution is intact. expanded_final_url rows containing http:// total 3,084 impressions, 108 clicks, £48.65 (24.8% of clicks), but that is how Google reports the URL and does not show users passed through an http hop; plain http is untestable from this sandbox (proxy 405). Measured cost over 3 runs: the apex leg needs its own TLS handshake (time_appconnect about 0.14 s, TTFB 0.25 to 0.30 s) before the www request (TTFB 0.12 to 0.31 s), so roughly 0.25 to 0.3 s per click, more on a mobile radio. The three gad_campaignid values differing from campaign_id are normal Performance Max reporting, not a defect. One edge 301 on a page whose simulated mobile LCP is 5.9 s is a real but modest loss; the fix (canonical www final URL) is correct and trivial, but high overstates it.

Reproduced on the live page in Playwright at 390x844 (isMobile) and 1440x900: document.querySelector('#Subject') has type 'tel', no inputmode, required true; the live markup is exactly <input class="input-field w-input" maxlength="256" name="Subject" data-name="Subject" placeholder="Subject" type="tel" id="Subject" required=""/>. The other fields are name text, email email, Phone tel (correct), Message textarea (not required). Screenshot shots/verify-1/contact-form-390.png shows a normal-looking text box; the defect only appears with a device keyboard. On iOS type=tel brings up the digits-only phone pad with no letter switch, so the intended free-text entry fails for iOS users; Android phone layouts likewise lack letters (paste or voice remain). However the field accepts any non-empty value, so a visitor can enter digits and submit, desktop is unaffected and the form itself works; it does not block conversion. A serious conversion defect on the paid landing page, so high, but critical is inflated.

Mechanics confirmed: a[href="tel:+447850522789"] carries classes 'c-social-card hide w-inline-block'; computed display none and a 0x0 box at 390x844 and 1440x900; the number appears nowhere in the rendered text; .c-social-wrap shows only info@roscap.co.uk and the @roscap.uk Instagram card (shots/verify-1/contact-390.png). conversion_action list has 6 website actions and none of a phone-call type. But 'hide' is Webflow's deliberate utility class, so this is a publishing choice (the owner may not want a public number) rather than a bug; the page still offers email and the form, and nothing in the data ties the missing number to lost paid conversions. Worth a decision from Clemente (publish the number or add a Book a call link) and a call asset if published, but medium rather than high.

Metrics confirmed from the Lighthouse JSON (contact-us mobile, fetched 2026-10-31T01:02Z, simulated slow 4G, 4x CPU): performance 0.67, FCP 2.3 s, LCP 5.9 s, Speed Index 3.7 s, TBT 330 ms, total 764 KiB, unused JavaScript 132 KiB; desktop 0.85 with LCP 1.3 s. lcp-breakdown-insight names img.hero-bg (412x873, loading=lazy) as the LCP element (observed TTFB 417 ms, load delay 408 ms, load 105 ms, render delay 130 ms) and lcp-discovery-insight fails both 'fetchpriority=high should be applied' and 'LCP resources shouldn't use loading=lazy'; the HTML has 0 rel=preload (the server does send a 103 Early Hint preloading the CSS). Live DOM: Vector-2.svg is 202 KiB, loading="lazy", no fetchpriority, bounding box top 0 height 873 at 390, so the lazy attribute on an in-viewport image is real. Two cause details are wrong or overstated. First, the four GSAP tags (gsap.min.js, SplitText, TextPlugin, ScrollTrigger) and jQuery plus the webflow chunks are synchronous scripts at the END of the body (character offsets 24,096 to 25,416 of 28,401; only gtag and Finsweet attributes sit in the head, both async), not site-wide head code, so they do not delay the first render of the hero; Lighthouse still lists them under render-blocking-insight (estimated savings 1,060 ms) because they are parser-blocking in the body, but their real cost is TBT and main-thread time (bootup 1.0 s, gtag 353 ms and webflow chunk 366 ms are the biggest), not LCP. Second, in my own Playwright Chromium run on the live page (390x844, 1.6 Mbps, 150 ms RTT, 4x CPU via CDP) the PerformanceObserver reported the H1 as the LCP element at 1,292 ms and never promoted the full-viewport SVG, so in current Chrome the SVG may not be the field LCP element and un-lazying it may move Speed Index more than LCP. The page is still slow on mobile for a paid landing page (score 67), so high stands; the fix list should say footer code rather than head code, and should lead with the lazy hero image, the 195 KiB gtag payload and the 132 KiB of unused JavaScript.

Core confirmed by re-pull: 6 conversion actions, generate_lead (SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM, ENABLED, primary, ONE_PER_CLICK, 90 d), Contact Us (GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_4_CUSTOM, category CONTACT, ENABLED, primary, MANY_PER_CLICK, 90 d), two GA4 purchase actions HIDDEN, qualify_lead and close_convert_lead HIDDEN; conversion tracking status CONVERSION_TRACKING_MANAGED_BY_SELF; enhanced_conversions_for_leads_enabled null; no 'AW-' string in any pre-fetched page or in the live DOM of / and /contact-us (Playwright), only gtag G-H8HS2R6NLS; no gtag('consent') call and no cookie-banner element. Two details are wrong: both conversion_tracking_setting_conversion_tracking_id and customer_conversion_tracking_setting_conversion_tracking_id return 238397354910, not 220059096840, and no Windsor field exposes a Google tag id, so 'AW-18338258070' has no source in the data (the setup log only records 'no Google Ads (AW-) tag'). The recommendation to add gtag('config','AW-18338258070') must not be implemented as written; read the tag id from Google Ads > Tools > Data manager > Google tag (the conversion tracking id 238397354910 points to AW-238397354910, to be confirmed in the UI). Double-counting risk from two primary actions is plausible but whether 'Contact Us' fires on the same submit was not verifiable. Severity high stands.

Rendered the F file via file:// in Playwright. At 390x844 (isMobile, hasTouch) #dl-pane (role=tabpanel, aria-live=polite) sits inside an li of ul.dl-list[role=tablist] before and after tapping row 3 (Rome, Bridge Loan); axe-core run on #track-record reports aria-required-children, impact critical, target .dl-list, 'Element has children which are not allowed: [role=tabpanel]'. Reproduced with gsap.getProperty on the odometer strips. At 1440x900: with the panel off screen the strips already show the final digits 3.75 / 3.75–4.00 / 2.618 and the chips are at opacity 1; 100 ms after the top-72% trigger every BoE and Fed strip is at 0 and EURIBOR at 2.638, chips at opacity 0 and visibility hidden; settled after 4 s. Scrolling to the top and back, 300 ms after re-entry the strips read 1.2,1.2,0 / 0,0,0,0,0,0 / 2,6,3,8 with chips hidden (shots/verify-1/rates-reenter-300ms-1440.png shows the Fed value as 0.00–0.00), and the same re-roll fires on re-entry from below (onEnterBack). At 390x844 the frame with the panel top at 74% shows 3.75 and the Held chip, and the frame at 70% shows 0.00 with the chip hidden (rates-seq-74-390.png, rates-seq-70-390.png), so the value-to-zero snap is real. Reduced motion shows final digits immediately. Mechanism matches the code (ST.create with onEnter and onEnterBack and no once; buildOdo presets final digits; fromTo on the chips with delay 1.1 renders the from state immediately). Severity: the values are correct at rest within about 2 s and nothing is misreported, so this is a noticeable motion polish issue (medium) rather than one that clearly hurts trust or accessibility; the once:true, start-state and earlier-trigger fixes are right.
